facet_contributions.possible_uses: Helps explain the technical considerations in studying the mechanism of action involving microbial metabolites. It underscores why accurate quantification is necessary to understand host-microbe interactions.

paper_identity.title: Enhanced Detection of Short-Chain Fatty Acids Using Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometry

planning_summary: This paper provides a technical methodology for measuring short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), which are key microbial metabolites. While it does not directly address the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) or solid tumors, it offers a critical tool for quantifying the 'gut microbiome' output (SCFAs) that may mediate ICI efficacy. It serves as a reference for how SCFA levels can be accurately measured in human serum and feces, which are common biomaterials in oncology and immunology studies.
scope_interpretation_cautions: This is a methods paper; do not interpret its protocol description as evidence of biological findings regarding ICIs or solid tumors.
The 'proof-of-concept' nature of the 14 SCFAs means the method may not cover all relevant microbial metabolites discussed in broader ICI reviews.
Ensure that any use of this paper in the review clearly distinguishes between the *measurement capability* (this paper) and the *biological correlation* (other papers).
topic_handles: Sample preparation protocols (alkaline extraction, MTBSTFA derivatization)
